t.E243.agn: In 2019 EFSA maintained the existing ADI of 0.5 mg/kg body weight and did not accept a proposal to increase it. It reported that at the current permitted level (160 mg/kg) this limit could be reached in high-consuming toddlers and children, and that with the proposed new uses it would be exceeded at average consumption in all age groups.
t.E243.body: After ingestion it is completely broken down into L-arginine and lauric acid, which are normal products of metabolism.
t.E243.eff.0.a: At the current permitted level (160 mg/kg)
t.E243.eff.0.t: The daily limit may be reached
t.E243.eval: A preservative in heat-treated meat products; in the body it is broken down into L-arginine and lauric acid. In 2019 EFSA maintained the ADI at 0.5 mg/kg body weight/day; it reported that at the permitted level (160 mg/kg) this limit could be reached in high-consuming toddlers and children.
t.E243.found.0: Heat-treated meat products (except emulsified and smoked sausages and liver pâté)
t.E243.prod: Produced by chemical synthesis by esterifying arginine with ethanol and reacting it with lauroyl chloride.
t.E243.pw.0: According to EFSA, the daily limit may be reached in high-consuming toddlers and children at the current permitted level.
t.E243.regx.0: ADI of 0.5 mg/kg body weight/day maintained; the proposed extension of use was not supported because it would lead to the ADI being exceeded.
t.E243.summary: A preservative made from the amino acid arginine and lauric acid. It prevents bacterial growth in meat products and cheese.
t.E243.what: It is a preservative that limits bacterial growth in heat-treated meat products.
